name: Dependency Tracking Agent
problem: Knowing which tests exercise which production classes requires observing real execution, not just static analysis
how: A java.lang.instrument agent records class loads within each test's execution window, attributing runtime-loaded classes back to the test that caused the load

name: Selection Engine
problem: Deciding which tests to run for a change needs multiple explainable strategies, not one opaque rule
how: Composes independent selectors (dependency-match, fallback, new/modified-test), each attaching an explicit SelectionReason to every test it selects

name: Conservative Fallback
problem: Test selection must never silently skip a test that could catch a real regression
how: Changed files are classified by FileKind; anything ambiguous or non-source-attributable widens the selected test set instead of narrowing it (sound-by-default)

name: Dependency Index
problem: Tracked test-to-class dependencies must persist and be safely reused across CI runs without going stale or format-incompatible
how: A versioned, commit-keyed index is persisted locally and checked for reachability/format-applicability before reuse; unreachable or incompatible indexes fall back conservatively

name: Reactor Module Graph
problem: Fallback rebuilds/selection should scope to affected modules, not always widen to the whole multi-module reactor
how: The module graph is derived from the git tree (not the build tool's runtime reactor), treating <parent> POM references as dependency edges; unattributable paths default to reactor-wide

name: Shadow-mode Validator
problem: The selection engine's soundness (never missing a test that should run) needs independent, evidence-based verification
how: Replays historical commit pairs, builds ground truth via an unmodified full test run, and can inject bounded synthetic mutations to measure would-miss coverage

name: Build-tool Integration (Maven & Gradle)
problem: Developers need test selection wired into their existing build without changing their workflow
how: The Maven plugin routes one goal among TRACK/SELECT/FALLBACK via a mojo; the Gradle plugin computes selection immediately before the Test task executes
